ADVISORY (not yet blocking this task) — F22 (P1, OPEN, NEW, tenth PR #325 Copilot review, HEAD 914cb214).

Plan §3.2 terminates three post-`LOCKING` failure edges (BOOTSTRAPPING fatal, RESOLVING no-copilot-exe, LAUNCHING spawn-error) directly at FAILED without passing through DRAINING — and DRAINING is where the plan places LOCK RELEASE. Combined with this task's own fail-closed stale-lock policy (§3.4: stale lock requires an explicit operator `--force-unlock`, never auto-broken), a routine pre-RUNNING failure leaves the workspace permanently locked until the operator finds and runs --force-unlock.

WHY THIS TASK IS IMPLICATED EVEN THOUGH THE DEFECT IS IN THE STATE MACHINE: the operator has two ways to close the hole. (1) Fix the transition table in 119.003-T so every post-LOCKING terminal exit routes through DRAINING — this task is then unchanged, and the fix is confined to 128-S. (2) Put the guarantee HERE, making release structural rather than caller-dependent — e.g. acquisition returns a scope guard / context manager whose exit always releases, so no reachable termination path can leak the lock regardless of what the state machine does. Option (2) is the more robust design (it cannot be re-broken by a later transition-table edit) but it ADDS A DoD OBLIGATION AND TESTS TO THIS TASK, which is a member of 127-S — the otherwise-eligible first shipment.

This comment is recorded so that whoever implements T5 does not lock in an API that makes option (2) impossible. It does NOT by itself block 127-S; 127-S is already blocked by F17. Stage adopted no resolution and changed no dependency edge.
